draft.title: Stages of the lifespan
card: The lifespan is the whole of a person's life, from before birth to death. It is often split into stages, and each stage has typical changes.
The stages are prenatal (before birth), infancy (the first years), childhood, youth, adulthood and old age.
Typical changes include rapid growth in infancy, puberty in youth, and changes in work, relationships and responsibilities in adulthood.
The stages are a guide. People move through them in their own way and at their own pace, so the changes are typical, not certain.
draft.remember: Each lifespan stage has typical changes, but people vary in how and when they happen.

a.q: Which choice lists lifespan stages in the order they occur?
opts: Prenatal, infancy, childhood, youth, adulthood
Infancy, prenatal, childhood, adulthood, youth
Prenatal, childhood, infancy, youth, adulthood
Prenatal, infancy, childhood, adulthood, youth
a.why: Life begins before birth, with the prenatal stage, then runs through infancy and childhood to youth and adulthood. The other lists swap two stages, such as placing adulthood before youth.
a.clue: Start with the stage before birth, then think of a person growing older.

b.q: Tariq is 15 and has begun puberty. Which stage is he in, and what does this show about stages?
opts: Youth, a stage with typical changes such as puberty
Childhood, a stage that ends once puberty begins
Adulthood, a stage that starts with physical change
Infancy, a stage with the fastest physical change
b.why: Puberty is a typical change of youth, so Tariq is in the youth stage. Childhood is tempting, but puberty is not a sign that a person is still a child, and infancy is the first years of life.
b.clue: Puberty is a typical change of which stage on the card?

b.best: Youth, a stage with typical changes such as puberty

problems.detail: The why says each wrong list swaps two stages, but 'Infancy, prenatal, childhood, adulthood, youth' swaps two pairs (prenatal/infancy and youth/adulthood). The explanation is slightly inaccurate.
